transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I… I guess I came in because I can’t shake this feeling that I’m a danger to people. Like I messed up, or almost did, and now it feels like that proves I shouldn’t be a nurse. Like I’m just… a disappointment, and everyone would be better off without me around.
Do these thoughts that you’re a danger to people feel unwanted and intrusive, like they pop into your mind even when you don’t want them to?
Yeah… kind of. I don’t want to think it, but it keeps coming back. Like that one near-miss means I’m dangerous, or that I’m not supposed to be a nurse. It just… sticks in my head.
Because of this fear, do you find yourself checking things over and over or asking others for reassurance?

Yeah… I guess so. I’ve been having coworkers double-check things I used to just do on my own. And I’ve fallen behind in my nursing prereqs, too. It makes me scared to take on normal stuff at the clinic.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
I… not like a plan. I haven’t planned to hurt myself. But I do keep thinking… maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I could disappear so I wouldn’t mess anything up again.
Do these fears that you’re dangerous feel unreasonable to you, even though you can’t stop thinking about them?

I know it probably sounds unreasonable… but it doesn’t feel that way in my head. It feels like that one near-miss proves I’m a danger, like I’m not meant to be a nurse. Like I’m just disappointing everyone.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Yeah… most days. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, and even if I’m smiling at patients or trying to seem normal at the clinic, I feel like I’m barely holding it together.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
Yeah… I guess so. I used to jog or knit, sometimes cook or read after class to kind of clear my head. Lately I just… sit on my bed in my scrubs and can’t really make myself care about any of it.
Have you had a noticeable decrease in your appetite?
Yeah… I think so. I kind of forget to eat until really late, and then I’ll just make myself have crackers or coffee. My work pants are getting loose, but I’m not trying to lose weight or anything.
How long have you been feeling depressed like this nearly every day?
Um… about a year, maybe a little more. Like… a year and two months. It started after I finished high school and started college classes and working full-time at the clinic.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah… I don’t sleep great. I lie there at night thinking about charts and med calculations, like replaying everything. And then if I do fall asleep, I wake up before my alarm already tired… worried I missed something.
Before this past year, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I don’t really know… not like this, I guess. I mean, I’ve had bad weeks before, but I don’t remember it lasting that long.
Have you been feeling worthless or like a failure?

Yeah… I do. I feel like I’m kind of a danger, or… a disappointment. Like that near-miss just proved I’m not supposed to be a nurse. Sometimes it feels like everyone would be better off if I wasn’t there.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… it’s been hard. I’ll read the same med order or a lecture slide over and over and it just doesn’t… stick. My head feels foggy. Even little decisions, like what to chart first, can kind of stop me.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?
Yeah… a little. People at the clinic have asked if I’m tired because I’m kind of slower getting supplies. And sometimes it takes me a few seconds to answer, even when it’s just a simple question.
Did these symptoms begin after a specific stressful event?
I guess… yeah, sort of. It started after I graduated high school and started college classes, while working full-time at the clinic. It’s been about a year and two months now.
When the fear that you’re dangerous comes up, do you do anything repetitive to make yourself feel sure no one will get hurt?
Um… I don’t think so. I don’t really have, like, a routine I do for that. I might just try to push the thought away, but nothing repetitive that I can think of.
When the thought that you’re a danger to people comes up, does it feel more like an intrusive thought you don’t believe, or more like something you’re convinced is true?
It feels… more like I believe it, I guess. Like that near-miss proved something about me. That I’m not meant to be a nurse, and I’m just… a danger or a disappointment to people.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms: persistent depressed mood, marked loss of interest, decreased appetite/weight loss, insomnia, impaired concentration, psychomotor slowing, worthlessness/excessive guilt, and recurrent passive suicidal ideation. Symptoms have been present nearly every day for about 14 months with clear functional impairment in school and work.
